book: Make It Stick: The Science of Successful Learning

questions.q: [Sample] According to the Preface, what is the catch about the most effective learning strategies?
questions.explain: The authors say the most effective strategies are not intuitive, so people tend to choose weaker ones.

questions.section: Claims We Make in This Book
questions.q: True or false: [Sample] The authors claim that rereading text is one of the most productive study strategies.
questions.explain: They say rereading and massed practice are the favourite strategies but among the least productive.

questions.section: Claims We Make in This Book
questions.q: [Sample] Recalling facts or concepts from memory is called retrieval ____.
questions.explain: Retrieval practice is the authors' term for recalling learning from memory, for example with flashcards.

questions.q: [Sample] Which of these are benefits of retrieval practice described in the book?
options: It shows what you do not yet know
It removes the need for any effort
It works only on the day of the test
questions.explain: Retrieval strengthens memory and reveals gaps; the book stresses that effortful retrieval works best.

questions.q: [Sample] Put the steps of learning in the order the book describes them.
questions.explain: Information is encoded, consolidated into long-term memory, then retrieved when needed.

questions.q: [Sample] Sort these into massed practice and its more effective alternatives.
questions.explain: Cramming and rapid-fire repetition are massed; spacing and interleaving are the alternatives the book recommends.

questions.q: [Sample] Match each of Kahneman's systems to its description.
questions.explain: The book borrows Kahneman's two systems and defines metacognition as monitoring your own thinking.

questions.q: [Sample] In your own words, what is the testing effect?
questions.a: The testing effect is the finding that retrieving knowledge from memory makes it easier to recall later, so practicing retrieval makes learning stick far better than rereading the material.
